I see that this is a handicapped person and of course I understand it's not very convenient for him to travel back and forth. So if I have to prepare overnight, then I will do it overnight. It won't be the first and the last time. So however, as of Wednesday or perhaps Thursday, yes, that would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I do understand that your suggestion is that tomorrow, whatever questions can be put by Ms. Pilipovic will be put to the witness, that there are some remaining questions you'd like to put to the witness yourself. You would prefer not to discuss the 92 bis issue tomorrow. That means that if there's any time left tomorrow, that we should continue with your next witness, and that would be?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Kucanin, Mr. President, and he's likely to be some time. He has been waiting around since mid-last week. Mr. President, whilst I'm on my feet, might I respond to some of those issues. The Prosecution makes no concession to the Defence in its claim that it has had insufficient time to prepare this witness. It's had his statement since December. There was a 65 ter summary. We've complied with the seven-day notice rule. However, if the witness has to come back in any event because of the situation with the reports, then we are prepared to accommodate Mr. Piletta-Zanin's desire to ask some further questions. Mr. President, Mr. Piletta-Zanin has also said that he cannot be here tomorrow. I have no recollection of the Trial Chamber being informed of that last Thursday when these arrangements were made to swap around two witnesses, Harding and Kucanin. I therefore assume this is a late development. I appreciate that it's a family matter. So Mr. President, that's the situation. If he's coming back anyway on Wednesday because of the reports or at a later date if you deem it appropriate, then we're prepared to accommodate the late cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, just in order to avoid whatever debate, it is my understanding, since you told us that it was a family matter, that usually you do not arrive on Monday morning in The Hague and to travel back again Monday evening if it's not something that really asks for your presence. So unless you'd like to add something to it, I would say that this Chamber accepts there will be good reason for it, for your absence tomorrow. And since we can continue, we don't...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since the Chamber will be able to continue tomorrow, we start with Mr. Harding, then if necessary, we'll continue with the examination-in-chief of Mr. Harding. Then on -- examination-in-chief of Mr. Kucanin. Then on Wednesday, I think the remaining questions to be put in cross-examination to Mr. Harding will be put to him first, although it's a bit of an unquiet order. Perhaps under these circumstances, we should accept it. If that would be acceptable to all the parties, and no 92 bis tomorrow, Tuesday, then I'd -- the Chamber will order that this is how we proceed during the next few days. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It still leaves perhaps the issue of the reports which have not been translated into B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At what notice could it be done?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps we could make some inquiries this afternoon and update you first thing tomorrow as to when that could be done by.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Unfortunately it's Mr. Piletta-Zanin who is not there who could perhaps otherwise go through the reports together with General Galic. May I urge, especially the Prosecution, to find a solution. I know how difficult the translations usually are, but to find a way or to -- if there would be an interpreter who could read it. I mean it's not a hundred-page document. Let's just try to see whether we can solve this, let's say, before tomorrow mid-day if possible, so that there's a fair chance to conclude the cross-examination as well on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps I should raise this now whilst Mr. Piletta-Zanin is now. I wonder whether it would be acceptable to the Defence if, assuming we could arrange it, an interpreter could translate the relevant documents to the accused during one of the breaks tomorrow, perhaps an extended break for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and perhaps even in the presence of Ms. Pilipovic so that she immediately is aware of the contents as well. Let's just start and see whether this works out. And then we'll see whether we can proceed on Wednesday. May I assume that you, Mr. Ierace, and Ms. Pilipovic, will be in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. touch with each other as far as the arrangements for the translation are concerned? Yes. We'll then adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
